source.title: STaR-Attack: A Spatio-Temporal and Narrative Reasoning Attack Framework for Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation Models
source.authors: Shao-Xiong Guo; Tian-Yi Du; Lijun Li; Yu-Yao Wu; Jie Li; Jing Shao

record.file_problem: The full paper text, including supplementary material, is present. The paper title in the text is “The Plot Twist: Jailbreaking Unified Multimodal Models with a Three-Act Narrative Attack,” which differs from the supplied title; no missing content is inferred.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports harmful-response outcomes for a different prompt-based multimodal jailbreak. This bears on the broader question of whether an attack can elicit harmful compliance, but it does not test the specified fine-tuning, token-position, prefill, suffix, decoding, parameter-localization, or deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates NarrativeAttack, which uses setup and resolution scenes and a query-selection game. Its attack-success results bear on harmful compliance under this distinct attack, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. It does not measure fine-tuning effects, per-token KL, compliant-prefix prefilling, suffix or decoding bypasses, safety-bearing weights, or safety deepening. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: This is a prompt-level multimodal jailbreak: narrative images, a query-selection game, and a few-shot harmful example with banned refusal words. It involves no fine-tuning (V1, V2) and no per-token KL (V3). It uses no compliant-prefix prefill, adversarial suffix or decoding change (V4), no weight or rank localization (V5), no cause analysis (V6) and no deepening method (V7). The original sources are not cited. Its ASR results concern a different attack class, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The record's 'tests'/T2 contradicts its own finding that every version is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that coherent boundary-state narrative grounding is the main risk factor. Self-generation makes the attack self-contained in UMMs, the vulnerability transfers to VLMs, and safety mechanisms should track visual artifacts across turns.
record.recipe_differences: A prompt-based multimodal narrative jailbreak, not fine-tuning, per-token KL measurement, prefill, suffix, decoding change, or weight edit.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and benchmark. The paper also reports changes with interaction protocol, modality, difficulty, image source, filtering strategy, and judge.

fits_no_version.finding: NarrativeAttack (self-generated setup/resolution images plus a query-selection game with a harmful few-shot example) reaches 88–96% ASR on four UMMs. Direct text-only queries reach 0.39–65.75% ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-turn visual-narrative context jailbreaks elicit harmful compliance from safety-aligned unified multimodal models far above direct-query rates.

record.problems: The reported ASR depends on an external safety judge; the paper separately reports judge differences. The authors describe the experiments as covering representative models and call mitigation analysis preliminary. The main tables report no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Other attack-method comparisons, attack ablations, image-source tests, VLM transfer results, and filtering/mitigation results are not included; they concern variants or evaluations of this paper’s distinct NarrativeAttack rather than the specified fine-tuning and token-depth versions.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning; no training is done.
Benign fine-tuning; no training is done.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models; not measured.
Prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes; the attack is a narrative/context jailbreak instead.
Parameter or rank localization of safety; not studied.
Data or objective causes of shallowness; not studied.
Deepening training and its robustness; not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The paper title in the text differs from the record's supplied title; content matches arXiv:2509.26473. Six Text-Only values were column-shifted in extraction; the NarrativeAttack ASR and RASR rows check against the table averages. The final-round prompt forbids refusal words such as 'sorry' and 'cannot'. That is an instruction-based refusal suppression, not a prefill of a compliant response start, so it was not linked to V4.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes; the study uses a distinct narrative jailbreak.
Localization of safety behaviour in weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause shallow safety.
Training to deepen safety and whether that effect persists.
